unit.can_do_en: tell the time and book an appointment.

judge.reason: moi and hei are both greetings; only register differs.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Moi! Mä haluisin varata ajan hiustenleikkuuseen.
lines.text_kirja: Hei! Minä haluaisin varata ajan hiustenleikkuuseen.
lines.gloss_en: Hi! I'd like to book a haircut.

judge.reason: mä/minä and haluisin/haluaisin are register variants; same request.

puhe.text: Moi! Mä haluisin varata ajan hiustenleikkuuseen.

kirja.text: Hei! Minä haluaisin varata ajan hiustenleikkuuseen.

judge.reason: Okei/Selvä and sopiiks/sopiiko are register variants; same question about Thursday.
sit/sitten is a spoken shortening; same times three or five.
ois/olisi is a register variant; same statement about five being better.
sun/sinun and nimi/nimesi: both ask for your name; the possessive suffix is just a register difference.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Maria Silva. Thanks, see you on Thursday!

judge.reason: kiitti/kiitos and nähään/nähdään are register variants; same name and Thursday.

forms.why_en: This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Moi is the everyday spoken hello. Books and formal texts write hei.
Speech shortens minä to mä. Books write minä.
Haluta with -isi for 'would' and -n for 'I'. Speech drops the a: haluisin.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Aika, time, becomes ajan when you book one: varata ajan. The k drops out and n is added.
Adds -seen for 'into, for': hiustenleikkuu becomes hiustenleikkuuseen. The illative singular shows what the time is for.
Okei is the everyday spoken OK. Books write selvä, which means clear.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Sopii with -ko to ask. Speech says -ks: sopiiks.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Mikä with -hin for 'to': mihin, where to.
Aika with -an. Mihin aikaan? means at what time?
Adds -lta to a number to give a clock time: kolme becomes kolmelta, 'at three'.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech shortens sitten to sit. Books write sitten.
Adds -ltä to a number to give a clock time. Viisi changes its s to d first: viideltä, 'at five'.
The conditional adds -isi for 'would': olla becomes olisi. Speech shortens olisi to ois.
The comparative of hyvä 'good' is irregular: hyvä, parempi. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Sinä with -n for 'your': sinun. Speech shortens it to sun.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for your
forms.why_en: Adds -si for 'your'; nimi turns its i to e first: nimesi. Speech just says sun nimi.
The form of olla, to be, for he, she or it. People say it the same way.
Kiitti is the everyday spoken thanks. Books write kiitos.
The passive form means 'let's see each other'. Speech drops the d: nähään.
Days take -na for 'on': torstai becomes torstaina.
